That conjunct is carried by the stdio path: stdio_enabled_nonce_replay_then_fresh_batch_is_signed (tests/message_signing_stdio_coverage.rs:167) and stdio_enabled_optional_nonce_omitted_is_signed (:228) route through verify_signed_wire (:291) to an independent Node verifier doing createHmac("sha256") and timingSafeEqual (tests/common/signing_verifier.mjs:173, :212), with a fixed-vector unit at src/security/message_signing_v2_tests.rs:66. RESIDUAL GAP: no HTTP-transport test verifies a delivered MAC; the HTTP path is asserted by shape alone.

Regraded 2026-09-12: the 2026-09-12 MET grade is WITHDRAWN. It was established by module, not conjunct by conjunct, off a passing test count. A conjunct audit splits the criterion into seven parts and two of them have no covering construct. COVERED: principal/backend/resource keying for load (s01_independent_committed_fixture_resolves_every_account_axis, store_tests.rs:166), for save (s03_explicit_initialization_creates_encrypted_authority_and_reopens, tests.rs:272) and for refresh (invalidate_during_held_refresh_discards_stale_provider_success, service_refresh_tests.rs:102); at-rest protection (s02_envelope_roundtrip_has_exact_public_shape_and_no_plaintext_secrets, tests.rs:168 and s03_independent_aes256_gcm_vector_opens_exact_expired_payload, tests.rs:362, against seal_bytes at storage.rs:154 with 0o600 at commit.rs:81); no silent loss under crash (s10_a_committed_generation_survives_an_abrupt_death, crash_tests.rs:119). NOT COVERED: existing single-user data is READABLE - no test opens a pre-existing 3.x single-user store; and MIGRATED - no test, no code path, and the source states the opposite. src/personal_accounts/mod.rs:779 reads "Existing state is never replaced, and nothing is migrated into a store this command creates" and :790 "a store this creates has zero records by construction"; src/commands/upgrade.rs:243 ships the user-facing notice "Stored tokens from 3.x are not migrated: each OAuth backend re-authenticates once". legacy_migration (mod.rs:207) is a dead field, only ever written None (repair_tests.rs:179). This is an implementation gap, not a test gap: the row cannot reach MET by adding tests. Either the migration path is built, or the criterion is rewritten to match the shipped re-authenticate-once behaviour, which is an operator decision. The accounts_init_store.rs:117 local-only failure recorded by the previous note is unrelated and stands. Follow-up 2026-09-12: the two options are not symmetric, and the source says which way it leans. Not migrating is a deliberate shipped commitment, not an omission: it is item 1 of four in NOTICE_4_0_0_ITEMS (src/commands/upgrade.rs:241), a constant the comment at :238 says is pinned as a slice "so a test can assert the notice still carries every item". Building a migration therefore does not merely add a code path; it falsifies a release note the operator has already published to users and would have to be withdrawn from the notice, and it needs 3.x token material to be decryptable by 4.0.0 code that no longer keeps that format. Rewriting the criterion to match the shipped re-authenticate-once behaviour costs one requirement edit and leaves every other conjunct as graded. The recommendation is the rewrite; the decision is still the operator's, because it changes what MIK-6744 promised.
